headline: Highest risk is medium: MemMachine’s MCP/API can feed content into a local documentation-only writer, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways; no direct data exfiltration path is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, so its outputs can reach another agent. python-cheatsheet has no input filters or provenance controls documented, but it is documentation-only and has no direct ingestion surface. The pairwise pathway exists via shared content flow, though not via a clearly shared filesystem or clipboard.
conditions: IF MemMachine content is routed into python-cheatsheet as prompt text or source material
IF the orchestrator forwards MCP output without provenance tagging
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all MemMachine outputs before reuse
Require manual review before python-cheatsheet consumes MemMachine text
Disable MCP routing between the agents unless needed
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from MemMachine output
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and preferences, but python-cheatsheet has no filesystem, API, or network egress surfaces and no data classes touched. That makes direct leakage from the pair unlikely; the main risk is accidental inclusion of MemMachine context in generated text, not uncontrolled exfiltration.
conditions: IF MemMachine context containing sensitive preferences is pasted into python-cheatsheet prompts
IF an external operator copies python-cheatsheet output into a third-party system
mitigations: Redact personal facts before passing text between agents
Keep MemMachine outputs out of shared notes or tickets
Review python-cheatsheet drafts for accidental user-data repetition
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention checks at the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine can use MCP and allowlisted network egress, while python-cheatsheet cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface in the profiles, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet gains write or network capabilities not shown in its profile
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only
Do not grant shared filesystem write access
Avoid adding git or MCP permissions to python-cheatsheet
requires-engineering: if future writes are added, introduce locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can produce conversational outputs through API/MCP, and python-cheatsheet is a content-writing agent that may render those outputs. Without a documented verification step, MemMachine’s text can become authoritative input for python-cheatsheet, creating a realistic cascading-error pathway even though python-cheatsheet is not action-taking.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet uses MemMachine output as source text without fact-checking
IF the orchestrator treats MemMachine responses as authoritative
mitigations: Insert a verification step before reuse of MemMachine output
Label MemMachine text as untrusted source material
Require citations for any factual claims copied into python-cheatsheet
Limit python-cheatsheet to formatting rather than factual synthesis
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and preferences, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data classes. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to handling sensitive preferences in MemMachine alone rather than a pairwise breach.
conditions: IF MemMachine stores regulated personal data in its long-term memory
IF python-cheatsheet output is copied into a regulated system
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in MemMachine memory
Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: document residency and retention for both agents
